answer: One sack of grain, ground at one tide mill, buys a seat. A newcomer files a claim, the miller grinds one sack through a tide cycle, and the harbor master weighs the flour; a sack short by more than a pound fails, and a 400 POA bond burns. The millstone's quartz marks every sack, the meadow grows the grain, and one grinding costs $210, so 100 fakes need 100 sacks, $21,000 in fees and 40,000 POA in bonds; honest millers keep the nectar.
